The watchdog fires on /home, the user taps "Go to Home," that triggers router.replace('/') into index.tsx, which renders a Redirect but never marks itself painted since nothing calls markScreenPainted('/') — so eight seconds later the watchdog fires again on '/'. I shipped a recovery button that navigates straight into a route guaranteed to be flagged as blank, creating a self-inflicted infinite loop that I need to fix immediately.

I'm also noticing a race condition where index.tsx's auth check and the tabs layout's separate auth guard could fire competing navigations if the authenticated state flips during a profile fetch. {
  "tag_name": "v1.10.25-qa",
  "name": "IVX Holdings v1.10.25 — the black screen was route /",
  "draft": false,
  "prerelease": false,
  "body": "## I found the actual black screen. It is route `/`.

Not a theory. Four facts, each one printed straight out of the source:

```
1. the watchdog was allowed to judge '/'
   INSTRUMENTED_ROUTES = new Set<string>(['/', '/home', '/login']);

2. NOTHING in the entire app ever reported a paint for '/'
   app/login.tsx:2240      markScreenPainted('/login')
   app/(tabs)/home.tsx:336  markScreenPainted('/home')
   -> keys reported: /home, /login.  '/' NEVER reported.

3. route '/' rendered ZERO pixels on every decision branch
   app/index.tsx:55   return <Redirect href="/(tabs)/home" />
   app/index.tsx:61   return <Redirect href="/login" />
   app/index.tsx:65   return <Redirect href="/(tabs)/home" />
   <Redirect /> renders null.

4. and v1.10.24's recovery button navigated the user straight onto it
   const ROOT_ROUTE = '/';
   router.replace(alreadyHome ? ROOT_ROUTE : '/(tabs)/home');
```

**`<Redirect />` renders `null`.** So from the moment route `/` mounted until the router actually committed the destination, the app painted the root view's `#0A0A0F` background and nothing else. If the destination never committed — auth still resolving, router not mounted yet, or the tabs auth guard firing a competing `router.replace('/login')` that cancels it — that empty container stayed on screen with no error, no log, no crash.

That is the 14 continuous seconds of `rgb(12,8,14)` your recording measured. Not a rendering glitch. A route whose entire job was to render nothing.

## And my last build made it a trap

Because `/` was instrumented but could never report a paint, it was **guaranteed** to be declared blank 8 seconds after landing on it — by construction, every single time. v1.10.24's recovery button sent you there deliberately to force a remount. Tap recovery, wait 8 seconds, get accused again. I built that loop. It shipped yesterday.

## The fix — structural, not a timing tweak

Route `/` now **always renders visible branded content**, and the redirect rides alongside it instead of replacing it:

```tsx
return (
  <View style={styles.container} testID="index-route">
    <Text style={styles.brand}>IVX</Text>
    <ShimmerIndicator size="large" color="#FFD700" />
    <Text style={styles.status}>
      {destination === null ? 'Preparing your account…' : 'Opening IVX Holdings…'}
    </Text>
    {destination !== null ? <Redirect href={destination as never} /> : null}
  </View>
);
```

And it reports its paint honestly:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  markScreenPainted('/');
  return () => markScreenUnmounted('/');
}, []);
```

If the destination never commits, you now see the IVX loading screen — not a black void. The route cannot be an empty container on any branch, and recovery can no longer loop into an unanswerable accusation.

## The invariant that would have caught this before it shipped

```ts
for (const route of routes) {
  expect({ route, reported: ... }).toEqual({ route, reported: true });
  expect({ route, released: ... }).toEqual({ route, released: true });
}
```

**Every route the watchdog may judge must have a screen that reports a paint for that exact key.** `/` violated it for three builds. It is now enforced at build time.

That test caught a real bug in itself on first run: scanning raw source, a **doc comment** that merely mentioned the call satisfied the invariant — a false pass that would have let this exact defect through a second time. It now strips comments and scans code only.

6 new tests total, including runtime proof that `/` is judged blank before it mounts, safe once it paints, and judged again after it unmounts.

## Validation

- `runChecks` (TypeScript + lint + structure): **0 errors**
- Home + routing + crash-shield suites: **46 pass / 0 fail** (was 40)
- Full suite: **1192 pass**, 3 pre-existing unrelated failures (unchanged)

Verified inside the shipped bundle: stamp `1.10.25 (123)`, `index-route` present, `(tabs)/(home)` still absent, all prior layers intact. The two new status strings contain a `…` character, so Hermes stores them in its UTF-16 string table — decoded straight out of the binary at offsets 4019396 and 4027120: `Opening IVX Holdings…` and `Preparing your account…`.

versionName 1.10.25 / versionCode 123

`/` was judged by the watchdog but could never report a paint. Landing on it for
8 seconds **always** produced "Screen failed to load" — by construction, every
time. v1.10.24's recovery button navigated there deliberately to force a
remount, so: tap recovery → land on `/` → accused again 8s later. That loop was
introduced by the previous fix.

## 3. Fix — structural

`app/index.tsx` now always renders visible branded content, with the redirect as
a **sibling** of that content rather than a replacement for it:

```tsx

    <Text style={styles.brand}>IVX</Text>
    <ShimmerIndicator size="large" color="#FFD700" />
    <Text style={styles.status}>
      {destination === null ? 'Preparing your account…' : 'Opening IVX Holdings…'}
    </Text>
    {destination !== null ? <Redirect href={destination as never} /> : null}
  </View>
);
```

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  markScreenPainted('/');
  return () => markScreenUnmounted('/');
}, []);
```

The route cannot be an empty container on any branch, and recovery can no longer
loop into an unanswerable accusation.

```ts
for (const route of routes) {
  expect({ route, reported: ... }).toEqual({ route, reported: true });
  expect({ route, released: ... }).toEqual({ route, released: true });
}
```

Every route the watchdog may judge must have a screen reporting a paint for that
exact key. `/` violated it for three builds. Now enforced at build time.

**The test caught a bug in itself on first run:** scanning raw source, a doc
comment that merely mentioned the call satisfied the invariant — a false pass
that would have let this defect through a second time. It now strips comments
and scans code only.

once painted, and judged again after unmount.
